lineage_binding.wire_rule: Persist exactly one canonical UTF-8 JSON wrapper with exact keys {attempt,binding_id,envelope,predecessor_blob,predecessor_generation}; reject duplicate/unknown/missing keys, non-canonical encoding, non-uint attempt/generation, malformed predecessor blob, or binding mismatch. The nested envelope must independently satisfy decoder D0-D5 byte canonicality.
lineage_binding.attempt_rule: A lineage record is current only when attempt equals the current checkpoint's exact expected_attempt. A committed transition changes checkpoint identity before any later replay can be current; a validation failure performs no CAS1/CAS2 and leaves no falsely consumed transition.

lineage_verifier.rule: Strictly decode one canonical lineage wrapper; syntax, duplicate-key, unknown-key, missing-key, type, integer-domain, or canonicalization failure -> F_LINEAGE_MALFORMED; mutation=false.
Require nested envelope bytes to pass predecessor decoder D0-D5 exactly; failure -> predecessor malformed sink; mutation=false.
Require predecessor_blob to equal the exact current checkpoint blob selected for this transition; mismatch -> F_STALE_PREDECESSOR; mutation=false.
Require predecessor_generation to equal the current checkpoint's lineage_generation (migration seed 0 only for the named predecessor blob); mismatch -> F_GENERATION_MISMATCH; mutation=false.
Require attempt to equal the current checkpoint's expected_attempt; mismatch -> F_ATTEMPT_MISMATCH; mutation=false.
Recompute binding_id from the domain-separated tuple and require exact equality; mismatch -> F_LINEAGE_DIGEST; mutation=false.
Only after L0-L5 succeeds may the canonical envelope reach D6, V0-V6, and ordered guards G1-G11.
CAS1/CAS2 remain reachable only through L0-L6 plus the predecessor semantic verifier. Any lineage failure returns mutation=false before either CAS.
A successful successor checkpoint increments lineage_generation, thereby changing both persisted content and lineage identity even if the logical state token later returns to an earlier value.

proofs.stale_replay_fail_closed: After any successful successor commit, the current checkpoint blob and lineage_generation differ from the replayed record's bound predecessor. Therefore L2 or L3 rejects the replay before D6/V/G and before CAS1/CAS2. Before any successful commit, replay is the same still-pending transition rather than a stale committed predecessor; CAS still arbitrates the single predecessor update.
proofs.aba_like_predecessor_reuse_fail_closed: Logical state-token equality is insufficient for lineage equality. Every successful successor increments lineage_generation and persists it, so an A→B→A logical cycle has a different generation and therefore different bound tuple. Even if non-lineage payload bytes recur, L3 and L5 reject a record from the earlier A generation.
proofs.torn_or_truncated_persistence_fail_close: A truncation or byte splice that breaks UTF-8/JSON/key/type/canonical structure fails L0 or nested D0-D5. A syntactically valid mix of fields from different lineage records fails L5 unless all committed tuple components and envelope bytes are mutually consistent. A wholly old intact record is a replay and is rejected by L2/L3 after successor commit. None of these paths reaches CAS1/CAS2.
proofs.attempt_binding: The binding digest commits attempt together with predecessor identity and canonical envelope. Reusing a record under a different expected attempt fails L4; changing only the attempt or envelope without recomputing the binding fails L5. This prevents representational aliasing from creating a second lineage-valid CAS path.
proofs.no_new_external_semantics: The layer only rejects invalid persisted transition inputs. It does not claim to observe or atomically couple any external side effect, so the existing accept-no-ack missing capability remains unresolved.
